native_notes.text:
As a reminder, do your workout comments going forward like this:

1. Workout Readiness - (e.g. 6/10; couldn't fall asleep bc of stress)
2. Workout Execution - (e.g. 5/10; skipped last set after going too hard in the first set)
3. Nutrition - (e.g. 5/10; didn't eat during my hard 2 hour interval ride, but did eat before and after)
4. Misc - (e.g. lower back acting up again)

1-3: Rate out of 10 (10 is the best); add details if possible; e.g., "I ate two 50g carbohydrate bars" or "Felt sluggish to start" etc.
Misc: Have at it, or don't.
native_notes.title: How To Comment On Workouts

native_notes.text:
Week 0. The plan starts Monday. Arrive rested: sleep, normal riding if you have it, nothing heroic.

This block: Seven weeks to Shawangunk Grit (50 mi, 4,000 ft, New Paltz). Durability on the Saturday long ride, controlled threshold and climbing-repeat work midweek, one dress rehearsal, then a real taper.

Nothing to prove this week. Turn up Monday rested and with the bike working.
native_notes.title: Week 0: Pre-Plan

native_notes.text:
Week 1 of 7. Base. Nothing flashy; I want steady work and the point is accumulation.

Descending-Cadence Ladder Friday: power stays flat, the gear changes. Low rungs load the legs, high rungs teach them to spin. Watch the knees on the low stuff.

Base - + Time in the drops Saturday is the long one. Boring on purpose. I want fuel from the first twenty minutes, not when you get hungry.

The fitness is in the weeks you don't notice.

Watch the easy days. If they creep up in pace, the hard days will start falling short.
native_notes.title: Week 1: Base

native_notes.text: Legs heavy today is the load landing, not a warning sign.
native_notes.title: Week 1: Midweek

native_notes.text: I want the long ride fueled from hour zero, not when you get hungry.
native_notes.title: Week 1: Fuel The Long Ride

native_notes.text:
Week 2 of 7. Last load week of this block. I want the key sessions done properly; a reset follows.

Ronnestad 40-20 Tuesday. The short recoveries are the trick: I don't let you fully recover, so the oxygen system stays pinned without the legs blowing up.

Castles in the Sand Z4/Z3 x 4 Thursday: sustained work at the edge. Hold the number, do not chase it; the last interval should feel like the first, only later.

Sleep is the variable you control. I want seven hours minimum this week, more after the hard days.
native_notes.title: Week 2: Base

native_notes.text: If today feels flat, that is the last two hard days still in your legs. I expect that. Normal.

Float Sets Tuesday is the hardest thing this week. Start the first rep at the number, not above it, and let the set get hard on its own.

Missed work stays missed. Do not stack two hard days to make up a session.

Week 5 of 7. Build. The intensity is specific now and the long rides have a purpose I have chosen. This is where the race gets made.

Mixed Intervals Tuesday. If the power fades more than ten percent, the set is over. Ending early is correct; grinding out junk reps is not.

Descending-Cadence Ladder Wednesday is skill work, not fitness work. Smooth circles at every cadence; the rpm targets are in the workout.

If a hard session falls apart, stop and message me. One bad workout is data; two is a pattern.

High Cadence Intervals Wednesday again. Same rungs, and by now the low-cadence ones should feel like strength, not struggle.

Feeling sluggish in a taper is normal. Feeling sharp by the weekend is the goal. Do not add work to fix a bad day.

Race week. Monday, Thursday, Sunday off. Openers before Shawangunk Grit. Saturday is the assignment.

No bonus miles or make-up work. Keep the openers controlled. Fuel Shawangunk Grit with familiar products at 60-74 g/hr.

Inside or out—keep the written RPE smooth. Pain, illness, or changed function: stop and tell me.

workouts.title: Descending-Cadence Ladder

workouts.description:
FUEL:
Target 60g carbs/hr. Practice this prescription.
MAIN SET:
- 15min @ 65% FTP (Z2, RPE 3)
- 3 x (0:30 @ 120% FTP (Z5+, RPE 8-9) + 3min @ 105% FTP (Z5, RPE 8-9) + 8min @ 85% FTP (Z3, RPE 5-6) + 40min @ 66% FTP (Z2, RPE 3))
- 0:30 @ 120% FTP (Z5+, RPE 8-9)
- 3min @ 105% FTP (Z5, RPE 8-9)
- 8min @ 85% FTP (Z3, RPE 5-6)
- 39min @ 66% FTP (Z2, RPE 3)
- 10min @ 50% FTP (Z1, RPE 3)

RACE SIMULATION — ACT 1 OF 2

THE UNIT: 0:30 @116-124% (attack the base) → 3:00 @102-109% (sustain the climb) → 8:00 @83-88% (tempo over the top) — this is the crux demand of the race: attack a shorter climb, sustain it, then hold tempo over the top.

THE SHAPE: 4 units across 2.6hr of Z2 — Act 1 of 2. Each act packs them tighter; I've built it so race day is the only day you do the full count.

AUDIBLE: if the legs are gone after unit 3, skip the remaining attacks and ride the climbs at tempo — then finish the Z2.

workouts.description:

WARM-UP:

PROGRESSION:
-Level 5/6: Advanced - High training load, pushing limits
-Blended VO2max and G Spot. Combines 30/30 VO2 intervals with sweet spot work in the same session. This format builds both max aerobic power and sustainable race pace in one efficient workout. Level 5: Extended sets. More work per set. This is where real adaptations lock in.

EXECUTION:
-Follow every zone change as written and let the recovery steps come all the way down. Make each transition clean before adding pressure.

workouts.title: Muscle Recruitment Progressions - Trainer

workouts.description:
FUEL:
Target 67g carbs/hr. Practice this prescription.
MAIN SET:
- 15min @ 65% FTP (Z2, RPE 3)
- 3 x (0:30 @ 120% FTP (Z5+, RPE 8-9) + 3min @ 105% FTP (Z5, RPE 8-9) + 8min @ 85% FTP (Z3, RPE 5-6) + 40min @ 66% FTP (Z2, RPE 3))
- 0:30 @ 120% FTP (Z5+, RPE 8-9)
- 3min @ 105% FTP (Z5, RPE 8-9)
- 8min @ 85% FTP (Z3, RPE 5-6)
- 15min @ 66% FTP (Z2, RPE 3)
- 0:30 @ 120% FTP (Z5+, RPE 8-9)
- 3min @ 105% FTP (Z5, RPE 8-9)
- 8min @ 85% FTP (Z3, RPE 5-6)
- 32min @ 66% FTP (Z2, RPE 3)
- 0:30 @ 66% FTP (Z2, RPE 3)
- 10min @ 50% FTP (Z1, RPE 3)

RACE SIMULATION — ACT 2 OF 2

THE UNIT: 0:30 @116-124% (attack the base) → 3:00 @102-109% (sustain the climb) → 8:00 @83-88% (tempo over the top) — this is the crux demand of the race: attack a shorter climb, sustain it, then hold tempo over the top.

THE SHAPE: 5 units across 2.8hr of Z2 — Act 2 of 2.

3x 4x (30sec @ 150% / 30sec @ 60%) w/5min reco
--
30/30s target both your Anaerobic and VO2 Max power. These over/under efforts allow to recover from the high-power surges, while also stressing your VO2 Max system due to the short recoveries. The intensity of this session is very high, but each interval will go by quickly.

workouts.title: Pre-Race Openers

workouts.description:
RACE DAY: Shawangunk Grit
Date: 2026-11-07

FUELING PLAN:
- Carbs/hour: 67g (range: [60, 74])
- Total carbs: 239g over race
- Start fueling at 20 min, every 20-30 min thereafter
- Pre-race: 100-150g carbs 3-4 hours before start

PACING STRATEGY:
- First 30 min: EASY. Let others burn matches -- I want you playing the long game.
- Mile 10-40: Find your rhythm. Target G SPOT zone (88-94% FTP) on climbs.
- Final third: this is where you pass people. Increase effort as others fade.
- Technical sections: Smooth > Fast. Avoid mechanicals.

COURSE INTEL:
- Surface: About 98-99% gravel once you enter Mohonk Preserve at mile two: historic carriage roads, rough and steep in spots, loose rock especially on the descents. Two miles of public road behind a pace car at the start.
- Features: Lenape Climb (Strava-timed segment: 1.47 mi, 433 ft, 5.
